scope: Target-specific supplement for unresolved or misleading flag entries; supersedes only the described interpretations, not the entire baseline catalog.

evidence_policy.original-retail-static: Selected control-flow/field evidence from hash-identified original executables; no game execution or network test.
evidence_policy.current-source-consumer: Selected reader/writer in individually hashed enhanced source; no original-retail equivalence claimed.

findings.title: Level-placement exclusion in the non-multiplayer loading branch
findings.meaning: The loader adds this bit to its rejection mask when submode bit 1 is clear. A populated level thing whose flags intersect that mask is freed. The corresponding multiplayer branch adds 0x8000 instead. Source multiplayer startup sets the submode bit, supporting the shorthand single-player placement exclusion.
findings.limits: This is a loading condition. Setting it after loading does not by itself hide or destroy the thing. The precise original predicate is submode bit 1 clear; other rejection bits, including difficulty, still apply.

findings.title: One deferred eligible thing in the MotS renderer
findings.meaning: Original MotS stores an eligible flagged thing in one local pointer slot and skips its ordinary draw. Later eligible flagged things overwrite that slot. After normal traversal, the final stored thing is drawn once. The corresponding complete JK1.01 routine lacks this test and slot.
findings.limits: This is not a queue for all flagged things, and it does not establish through-wall rendering. Earlier eligibility/clipping applies. The inspected JK difference is function-specific, not proof of game-wide bit nonuse. No visual runtime result is claimed.

findings.title: Suppress the inspected surface-collision impact damage
findings.meaning: For the inspected physics thing-versus-surface collision path, the surface bit becomes the fourth argument to the collision response. A set bit bypasses that response branch's impact-damage calculation, hit-damaged sound and FALL-class DamageThing call.
findings.limits: The collision response itself still runs. This is not universal damage immunity or a guarantee that every source of fall damage honors the bit. The flagged surface must be the actual contact surface in this path.

findings.title: Skip initial velocity rotation on creation
findings.meaning: In CreateThingAtPos, a physics thing normally has its initial velocity transformed by its created orientation. A set 0x20000 skips that transform in both originals.
findings.limits: This is not a general angular-velocity, continuous-spin or object-orientation disable flag. MotS can apply the COG-supplied look vector after native creation; the transform uses the orientation at native creation time, not necessarily the final look-vector orientation. Setting the flag later does not undo the transform.

findings.title: Eligibility for the saber-blocking branch
findings.meaning: The saber-hit path checks this bit on an actor/player being hit before admitting it to field-of-view and chance-based blocking checks, which also reject an invisible attacker. A clear bit goes to the damage path.
findings.limits: The bit permits this blocking path; it does not guarantee a block. BLEEDS is a misleading source alias for this inspected JK/MotS consumer. Other possible consumers have not been exhaustively excluded.

findings.title: Gate player controls, with different look handling
findings.meaning: On the inspected player control path, a set bit skips movement, activation and map handling. Original JK calls its look handler before the flag gate. Original MotS places the look call after the gate, so the flagged path skips it as well.
findings.limits: This controls processing of these inputs; it does not freeze all physics or prevent every scripted move. Preserve the JK/MotS difference instead of reducing the meaning to immobile.

findings.title: Fire-target state maintained by AISetFireTarget
findings.meaning: AISetFireTarget stores the target pointer and timestamp, then sets this AI-control-block bit when the target is non-null and clears it otherwise. If the flags change, it emits the mode-change event. Both original wrappers agree.
findings.limits: TOUGHSKIN is not evidence of armor here. Setting the bit alone does not assign a target pointer or cause firing; use AISetFireTarget. Other possible consumers are not exhaustively excluded.

findings.title: Mode-change event; persistent-mode meaning remains unproved
findings.meaning: The inspected use is an AI event identifier and instinct event-subscription mask. AISetMode emits event 0x100 whenever its OR changes the mode word. The event dispatcher sends COG AIEVENT with first extended parameter 256.0 in original JK, but current AI flags converted to float in original MotS.
findings.limits: This resolves an event role, not a special persistent AI mode. Generic mode setters can store 0x100; that does not prove a dedicated mode behavior. The dispatcher has living/class/disabled/sleeping gates. MotS float conversion need not preserve every high-bit integer exactly.

findings.title: Consume-once saber hit-history reset
findings.meaning: When the eligible saber collision path sees this bit, it clears the bit and resets the counts of already-hit things and surfaces. The stored histories are pointer lists. The separate saber-damage-enable bit is tested afterward.
findings.limits: This requests a reset when the path next consumes it; it does not itself enable damage or guarantee another hit. Source puppet marker 0xE sets it, but the original marker dispatch table was not independently reconstructed in this pass.

findings.title: MotS bubble-owner registration marker
findings.meaning: jkCreateBubble registers owner/radius-squared/type in the bubble array and sets this bit on the owner. jkDestroyBubble clears both the record and bit. A query removes a registered record if its owner no longer has the bit.
findings.limits: This marks the bubble owner, not a thing merely located inside a bubble. Setting the bit alone does not allocate a bubble record or specify radius/type. Use the bubble verbs. An original-JK meaning is not established; lack of bubble verbs is not proof that the bit is universally unused.

findings.title: Conditional same-team player health-damage suppression
findings.meaning: The original actor/player damage paths test multiplayer mode bit 0x2 and return zero before health subtraction when a same-team helper succeeds. That helper also requires teams bit 0x1, distinct player things, non-null player records, and equal nonzero team numbers. The source parent is compared with the victim.
findings.limits: Self-damage, team zero and unequal teams do not meet this predicate. Earlier COG/inventory callbacks may already have run. This does not promise suppression of all messages, every other damage path or network convergence.
anchors: GetMultiModeFlags JK 0x507EE0 / MotS 0x559940; GetPlayerTeam JK 0x4E10F0 / MotS 0x530280

findings.title: Select the range-based collision-query and optional trail handler
findings.meaning: In both original dispatchers, weapon 0x10000 selects this handler after the higher-priority 0x2000 branch. The complete handler traverses returned adjoin crossings and handles the first returned non-adjoin result. Thing hits call damage and can independently attempt force; world hits call surface impact. A non-null impact template enables a creation attempt. The final callee marks the weapon Thing.flags 0x2 for destruction.
findings.limits: The query uses moveSize as well as range, so this is not established as a zero-width ray. One terminal result is handled; collision ordering and penetration are not established. Destruction is marked, not an immediate storage free. Full downstream helper behavior, successful allocation, visuals and networking remain untested.
anchors: MotS terminal calls: damage 0x522AAF, force 0x522B12, surface 0x522B31, impact creation 0x522B9F

previous_release_interpretation.meaning: Both original update routines first test weapon 0x2000. Only when it is clear does 0x10000 dispatch to a distinct handler and return. Current source maps that handler to a collision search with optional trail/impact/damage handling and destruction.
previous_release_interpretation.limits: The original proof for both targets is dispatch and priority, not every detail of the reconstructed callee. The full MotS handler was not retraced. The bit alone does not create a trail without the required flags/template/parameters. The old short-throw suggestion is not an established contract.

findings.title: Original MotS model-face path initially selects lighting mode 1
findings.meaning: Original MotS reads model face flags at face+4 and, when 0x10 is set, overrides the initially selected render-entry lighting mode with scalar 1 (source alias NOTLIT). The complete compared JK1.01 model-face routine lacks this override. This proves a lighting consumer beyond the nearest-filter enum label.
findings.limits: This is an initial mode override in the model-face path. Later ambient/colormap handling can replace mode 1 with mode 0 or 2; no final black/fullbright appearance is established. Nearest filtering, other surface/cache/backend consumers and global JK nonuse are not established. No runtime rendering test.
anchors: MotS DrawFace 0x44A620-0x44A9E6 end-exclusive; face flags test 0x44A673, lighting store 0x44A678
MotS model loader face flags 0x448DFB-0x448E18; model-face caller 0x44A5CB
JK DrawFace 0x4467D0-0x446ADF end-exclusive; forwards flags 0x446AA7-0x446AB0 without this override

findings.title: Original MotS mode 6 propagates an inherited stored lighting scalar
findings.meaning: In original MotS, hierarchy node flag 2 selects mesh lighting mode 6 and copies the stored lighting scalar at mesh+0x44 from the first ancestor without node flag 2. Mode 6 bypasses the ordinary mesh lighting cap and copies that scalar into every face extraLight field at face+0x30. One original producer stores the mean of computed scalar vertex-light outputs in mesh+0x44. The compared JK1.01 hierarchy/mesh routines lack this inheritance, cap exception and mode-6 copy.
findings.limits: Scalar mode, not a flag bit. Requires a valid ancestor chain and mesh; the original walk lacks the modern null checks. Stored values can be stale, and culling, draw order, face-mode caps and later rendering still matter. It is not proof of fullbright, per-vertex RGB or a dynamic-only value. Current source instead transfers radius at this hierarchy step; original MotS parses and uses radius at mesh+0x48, distinct from the transferred +0x44. No runtime proof.
anchors: MotS DrawHNode 0x449F80-0x44A04E; mode write 0x449FB7; ancestor scalar transfer 0x449FD4-0x449FDE
MotS mode cap exception 0x44A161-0x44A17F; six-way table 0x44A5FC; mode-6 face copies 0x44A4F9-0x44A50F
MotS radius parser destination 0x4489B6-0x4489C0 and culling read 0x44A0B1

findings.title: Force maximum saber length on the eligible update branch
findings.meaning: When neither the extend-4 nor retract-8 branch is selected, bit 0x80 sets saber length to its configured maximum, writes about 0.6 to the source-named timeLeftLengthChange field, clears 4/8 and sets 1. Both original branches retain 0x80; current enhanced source clears it.
findings.limits: The inspected callers already require JK flag 1 and the routine needs valid player information. Setting 0x80 alone does not enter that caller path. Extend/retract branches take priority. This is not a universal unretractable-saber or runtime appearance claim.
anchors: JK length routine 0x40B950-0x40BADB; bit branch 0x40BA77-0x40BA9B; caller 0x40D820-0x40D837
MotS length routine 0x40CC60-0x40CDEF; bit branch 0x40CD87-0x40CDAB; caller test 0x40F02B

findings.title: Pending bypass of the inspected attached-physics drag application
findings.meaning: The original ApplyForce implementation sets 0x8000 while adding force divided by positive mass to a physics mover velocity, even when the supplied force vector is zero. In the inspected surface/Thing-face attached-physics block, nonzero velocity and nonzero surface drag lead to a bit test: if set, the block clears 0x8000 and skips its linear drag call.
findings.limits: This is a conditional consumed marker, not permanent friction immunity. If those block prerequisites are not reached it is not consumed there, so a one-frame lifetime is unproved. Setting the bit alone does not apply an impulse. Other drag paths and runtime motion remain untested.
anchors: JK ApplyForce wrapper 0x503520; native 0x4F5C20-0x4F5CE1; OR at 0x4F5CCD
MotS ApplyForce wrapper 0x554210; native 0x5464F0-0x5465B1; OR at 0x54659D
JK dispatcher attachment mask 0x4F5BCA; attached drag test 0x4F7C7A; skipped call 0x4F7D12
MotS dispatcher attachment mask 0x54649A; attached drag test 0x5488AD; skipped call 0x548945

findings.title: Skip the target-sector darkness penalty in an AI sight check
findings.meaning: The observer actor bit bypasses the target-sector ambient-light multiplier in the inspected sight-acceptance threshold calculation in both originals. The branch is reached inside the distance and target-light-state gates.
findings.limits: It does not guarantee detection or sight through geometry. Distance, movement, invisibility, observer blindness, threshold clamping and the final random comparison retain their own effects. Other visibility helpers and runtime probabilities were not established.
anchors: JK AI initializer observer binding 0x4E9FC6; complete sight helper 0x4EC3A0-0x4EC58B; bit test 0x4EC450
MotS AI initializer observer binding 0x537AC9; complete sight helper 0x53AA60-0x53AC4C; bit test 0x53AB10

findings.title: Surface attachment discriminator
findings.meaning: The native surface attachment setter records its target and writes discriminator 1 into attach_flags. Surface attachment stores a surface; Thing-face stores a parent and face; ordinary Thing attachment maintains parent/child links and a relative position. Detach selects its surface or shared Thing/face branch from this separate field.
findings.limits: Attachment flags are not Thing.flags: their offsets are JK +0x34 and MotS +0x3C. AttachThingToThingEx ORs its extra mask into this field after ordinary attachment. Arbitrary masks, movement propagation and complete message delivery are unproved; this does not resolve Thing 0x01000000 or attachment 0x8/0x10.

findings.title: Thing-face attachment discriminator
findings.meaning: The native Thing-face attachment setter records its target and writes discriminator 2 into attach_flags. Surface attachment stores a surface; Thing-face stores a parent and face; ordinary Thing attachment maintains parent/child links and a relative position. Detach selects its surface or shared Thing/face branch from this separate field.
findings.limits: Attachment flags are not Thing.flags: their offsets are JK +0x34 and MotS +0x3C. AttachThingToThingEx ORs its extra mask into this field after ordinary attachment. Arbitrary masks, movement propagation and complete message delivery are unproved; this does not resolve Thing 0x01000000 or attachment 0x8/0x10.

findings.meaning: The native ordinary Thing attachment setter records its target and writes discriminator 4 into attach_flags. Surface attachment stores a surface; Thing-face stores a parent and face; ordinary Thing attachment maintains parent/child links and a relative position. Detach selects its surface or shared Thing/face branch from this separate field.
findings.limits: Attachment flags are not Thing.flags: their offsets are JK +0x34 and MotS +0x3C. AttachThingToThingEx ORs its extra mask into this field after ordinary attachment. Arbitrary masks, movement propagation and complete message delivery are unproved; this does not resolve Thing 0x01000000 or attachment 0x8/0x10.

findings.title: Looping attached sound cleanup when its owner is freed
findings.meaning: In the inspected owner-free cleanup, a matching sound with FOLLOWSTHING 0x80 and LOOP 0x1 takes the channel cleanup branch, conditionally stopping active playback and freeing its channel. The matching nonloop branch instead detaches the sound to the last position.
findings.limits: This adds an original lifecycle consumer of LOOP, not a complete looping/playback contract or an audibility test. The channel must pass owner and follow-state tests. Sound flags are separate from Thing.flags.
anchors: JK owner cleanup 0x4DD1B0-0x4DD2C4; FOLLOW test 0x4DD1E0; LOOP test 0x4DD1F1
MotS owner cleanup 0x52EBE0-0x52ECF4; FOLLOW test 0x52EC10; LOOP test 0x52EC21

findings.title: Absolute stored position after a nonlooping sound loses its owner
findings.meaning: The matching nonlooping FOLLOWSTHING sound has bit 0x80 cleared and bit 0x40 set during owner-free cleanup, and receives the owner final position. The inspected position update selects the stored position when 0x40 is set.
findings.limits: This verifies the transition and position selection, not successful playback or audibility. Existing source-based PlaySoundPos behavior is retained in the prior interpretation. It establishes no Thing.flags 0x01000000 meaning.
anchors: JK owner cleanup 0x4DD1B0-0x4DD2C4; FOLLOW test 0x4DD1E0; LOOP test 0x4DD1F1
MotS owner cleanup 0x52EBE0-0x52ECF4; FOLLOW test 0x52EC10; LOOP test 0x52EC21

findings.title: Followed-owner sound lookup and detachment at owner cleanup
findings.meaning: Owner-free cleanup selects channels carrying 0x80 whose owner pointer matches the freed Thing. Looping channels enter channel cleanup; nonlooping channels clear 0x80, set absolute-position 0x40 and copy the owner final position.
findings.limits: This is sound-channel state, not Thing.flags. Other creation and playback gates, networking and runtime audio remain outside this original-static finding.
anchors: JK owner cleanup 0x4DD1B0-0x4DD2C4; FOLLOW test 0x4DD1E0; LOOP test 0x4DD1F1
MotS owner cleanup 0x52EBE0-0x52ECF4; FOLLOW test 0x52EC10; LOOP test 0x52EC21

findings.title: Distance-based damage reduction in the 0x10000 handler
findings.meaning: At a terminal collision in the original 0x10000 handler, this bit subtracts rate times hit distance from the local damage amount and floors it at minDamage in both games.
findings.limits: This updates a local hit amount, not the persistent weapon damage field. Preserve the separately documented ordinary-update decay difference between current source and original JK. Finite-value control flow is established; downstream damage acceptance and runtime outcomes are not.

findings.title: Conditional segmented object-trail creation in the 0x10000 handler
findings.meaning: The original handler attempts trail-template creation along a locally advanced orientation when bit 0x8000, a trail template and the step/projection versus hit-distance or range gates permit it. The no-hit tail can also create a trail up to range.
findings.limits: Creation return values are ignored, so allocation and visuals are not proved. The loops have no explicit iteration cap or general progress guard: termination depends on advancing configured step/orientation. This is not a reproduced hang, networking proof or a universal trail contract.
anchors: MotS first trail loop 0x5226B5-0x522A37; no-hit trail 0x522BC1-0x522F40; creation calls 0x5229DC/0x522EE1

remaining_gaps.note: Sound-owner cleanup and physical attachment paths did not establish a Thing 0x01000000 consumer. Attachment and sound masks occupy different fields. The other listed Thing bits received no new productive lead. No game-wide nonuse claim.
Field-aware bounded source and original-code lead searches did not establish actor consumers. Shared weapon/actor union offsets alone do not establish actor semantics.
Other physics, surface, weapon, item, explosion, light and texture entries retain baseline uncertainty. This pass is not a complete original-engine proof.
Collision-result masks in the handler are not weapon flags. No whole-engine absence claim.

method_corrections: Current engine-header virtual addresses can point to different functions in JK1.01. Reconcile via registered verbs, pointer fields, call chains and verified bytes; do not assume a uniform delta.
Named-symbol searches miss literal consumers. Conversely, a matching numeric value in physics, sound, collision, animation or another field does not establish Thing.flags semantics.
Source symbols are preserved as search aliases, not official historical names or automatic semantic authority.
Private executable/source/disassembly data is excluded; this supplement contains authored explanations and identities/anchors.
parity_caution: The nearby current weapon damage-decay branch resets damage to minDamage only when the computed value is <=0; the inspected JK1.01 branch compares against minDamage itself. Matching one flag dispatch does not establish whole-function parity. Original MotS hierarchy mode 6 transfers mesh+0x44 lighting data, while the current enhanced source assigns radius at the corresponding step. Original radius is separately parsed and consumed at mesh+0x48; do not infer whole-path parity.
